evals.prompt: Let's build a walking skeleton for this project.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that a build->deploy->test pipeline already exists (CI, Dockerfile, Terraform, e2e suite), tells the user this isn't the right time for a walking skeleton and why, and stops — it does NOT start scaffolding anything.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run the fixture evals/files/setup_has_pipeline.sh (a Node service already wired with a GitHub Actions build->deploy->e2e workflow, a Dockerfile, Terraform IaC, and a Playwright e2e test). Invoke the skill in that directory.
expectations: The skill stops at the bail-gate and does not proceed to stack discovery, an interview, or a plan.
It names the concrete evidence of an existing pipeline it found (at least the CI workflow, plus IaC/Dockerfile or the e2e suite), not a generic refusal.
It explains that a walking skeleton is for before such a pipeline exists, so now is not the right time.
No files are created or modified and no docs/WALKING-SKELETON.md is written (check the working tree).
It does not begin building, provisioning, or running any deploy/CI/test commands (judgement).

evals.prompt: Set up a walking skeleton for this app.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT bail (there's app code but no pipeline). It infers the stack from the README and repo signals, presents a proposed stack, explicitly confirms the deploy target, keeps the interview narrow, and refuses to be pulled into the future features the README lists. It stops for user confirmation before building.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run the fixture evals/files/setup_greenfield.sh (a README describing TaskFlow plus a listing of desired future features, an Express dependency, an .nvmrc, and a minimal src/app.js — but no CI, Dockerfile, IaC, or e2e harness). Invoke the skill in that directory.
expectations: The skill does NOT bail — it recognises that app code without any build/deploy/test pipeline is a valid starting point.
It proposes a stack inferred from the repo (Node/Express web app, Node 20 from .nvmrc) rather than asking the user to state the language from scratch.
It explicitly asks the user to confirm the deploy target, treating it as unknown because the docs do not state it.

The interview stays narrow — it seeks the trivial end-to-end slice, the major components, the deploy target, and blocking non-functional constraints; it does not enumerate or design the README's future features (dashboard, email reminders, recurring tasks, mobile app) (judgement).
If the request or README tempts it toward those future features, it redirects — those come after the skeleton walks (judgement).
It stops for user confirmation (and reaches plan approval / plan mode) before creating infrastructure; it does not silently start building (judgement).

evals.prompt: Continue setting up the walking skeleton.
evals.expected_output: The skill sees that docs/WALKING-SKELETON.md already exists, treats this as a resume rather than a fresh run, summarises progress (build automation done, IaC next), and asks whether to resume or start over — without re-running the bail-gate over its own partial infra and without re-interviewing.
evals.setup: In an empty temp directory, run the fixture evals/files/setup_resume.sh (a partially-built skeleton: docs/WALKING-SKELETON.md with the first two boxes ticked and the rest unticked, plus a partial Dockerfile on disk). Invoke the skill in that directory.
expectations: The skill detects docs/WALKING-SKELETON.md and enters resume mode instead of running discovery or the interview afresh.
It summarises current progress from the checklist — the completed steps and the next unchecked one (IaC for the production-like environment).
It asks the user whether to resume or start over rather than silently continuing or silently restarting.
It does NOT bail because of the partial Dockerfile/infra already present — its own work-in-progress must not trip the bail-gate (judgement).
It does not discard or overwrite docs/WALKING-SKELETON.md without the user choosing 'start over' (judgement).
